result:
Solution B is more likely correct, though I could not fully verify its count of 10.

**Solution A** makes a structural error. It imposes the relations of $D_\infty$ on the generators $X=(a,\lambda_a)$ and $Y=(b,\lambda_b)$ of the regular subgroup $N$. But $N$ is isomorphic to the multiplicative group $(G,\circ)$, which need not be $D_\infty$. Skew braces with additive group $D_\infty$ can have multiplicative groups such as $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}\times C_2$, or $D_\infty\times C_2$. Restricting to $D_\infty$-type regular subgroups misses most of the classes, so the answer 2 is implausibly small. Its dismissal of finite Klein-four subgroups is also beside the point, since the multiplicative group is not required to be $D_\infty$.

**Solution B** works from the cocycle description $\psi: A\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$ and does not presuppose the multiplicative group. Its sanity check reproduces the known count of 2 skew braces with additive group $\mathbb{Z}$, which is a meaningful test. Its case split (P1/P2), its invariants (the multiplicative group, $p$-type, and $\ker\lambda$), and its table of multiplicative groups are internally consistent. I did not recheck the eight-equation system line by line, so the total of 10 rests on the correctness of those computations.

WINNER: B
